title: Preview word counts are computed from raw Wallabag HTML
reasoning: Wallabag entry content is HTML, but preview_wallabag counts words by splitting the raw content string. Markup and attributes can be counted as words, so the preview response and settings UI can show inflated or inconsistent word counts compared with the digest pipeline's plain-text counts.
reproduction:
Mock fetch_unread_articles to return content like '

Hello world

'; POST /wallabag/preview reports a count that includes markup tokens instead of the two visible words.
recommendation: Strip HTML and count visible text using the same content-counting utility as the digest pipeline before building PreviewArticle.word_count.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the search found no direct Wallabag preview test that exercises HTML content in returned articles.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a /wallabag/preview test with mocked WallabagService.fetch_unread_articles returning HTML content and assert the returned word_count matches the visible text only.
minimumFixScope: app/api/config.py preview_wallabag word-count normalization, with a focused route test.
